headline: Maui County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

meeting.body: Maui County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee
meeting.voteItem: Amendment to restore an administrative fine of up to $5,000 per violation
meeting.summary: The committee voted 8–0 on Bill 100, which sets lobbyist rules, and heard an update on a study of County boards and commissions.
meeting.recap: The committee took up Bill 100 (2026), which would set registration, reporting and penalty rules for lobbyists.[[0:05:08]] The director said a lobbyist training requirement was removed from the bill.[[0:09:51]] The Board of Ethics wanted fines of up to $5,000 per violation, like the state.[[0:10:34]] A County lawyer said a $5,000 fine would be allowed under the County charter.[[0:26:02]] A motion was made to put the up-to-$5,000 fine back into the bill.[[1:26:09]] The committee voted 9–0 to widen one definition so the rules cover matters sent to the Planning Commission and votes on department heads.[[1:31:38]] The committee voted 8–0 on the main motion as amended, with one member excused.[[1:33:41]] A county commission gave an update on its study of County boards and commissions.[[1:35:29]] The commission chair said it reviewed 15 of the County's 37 boards.[[1:37:35]] The chair recommended sunset dates or regular reviews for boards, and a minimum staff support standard for each.[[1:43:45]] A student testified in support of making the Commission on Children and Youth led by youth.[[1:54:31]] The committee deferred the item, which was posted for no vote.[[2:32:44]]
decided: A motion to replace the bill with a revised draft (CD1) was made and seconded, and the captions do not clearly show a separate vote on it.
The amendment was moved and seconded, but the vote result is not clear in the captions.
The chair deferred the boards and commissions update item after asking for objections.
meeting.next: The chair said the full council will take up the bill very shortly. The director said she would ask the state whether it has ever given a $5,000 fine and report back.
